The latest dense five-case resweep still favored the default worker at `29.0347s`, with `phase_bias` losing at `30.7907s`, `all_true` at `29.8937s`, and `all_false` at `43.1369s` despite crushing `large/test_8.cnf`. Any future phase-policy work needs a better classifier than clause density or current literal-bias statistics alone.
``````md
10. The current local portfolio gate still matches only `large/test_8.cnf`. If that logic is revisited, benchmark any simplification or replacement against the current path over multiple exact-CLI repeats, because serial bias seeding and the two-process portfolio are already very close on single-run timings. The newest dense-worker sweep closes off the most obvious extension of that idea too: the high-density pure-3-SAT cases (`large/test_6.cnf`, `special/hard.cnf`, `medium/test_4.cnf`, `large/test_10.cnf`) do separate cleanly from `large/test_8.cnf` by density, but simple alternate workers still lost there. On the same five-case serial sweep, the retained default worker finished at `28.9875s`, while `restart_base=32` took `36.5529s`, `restart_base=128` `46.3689s`, `var_decay=0.94` `35.6389s`, `var_decay=0.96` `31.1810s`, and `all_true` `31.5186s`. The variants that crush `large/test_8.cnf` are still not dense-UNSAT specialists, so any future portfolio expansion needs a materially different alternate search identity than local restart/decay/phase tweaks.
11. Keep the new root pure-literal presolve narrow unless a stronger exact-CLI signal appears. The ungated version was a clear trap: even one root pure assignment could perturb the search path badly enough to blow up `large/test_6.cnf` and `large/test_8.cnf`, taking a same-day exact-CLI mixed slice from `22.2586s` to `25.1953s`. The retained gate at `>= 2` root assignments recovered that and improved the same-day mixed exact-CLI slice to `22.0635s`, while also improving the repeat-aware in-process full suite from `25.2549s` to `25.1541s`. But two repeat-aware exact-CLI full-suite reruns still landed at `27.7868s` and `27.6136s`, so the historical `27.1974s` exact-CLI best remains unbeaten. Future presolve work should treat low-yield root simplifications as search-path perturbations first, benchmark them against same-day exact-CLI slices before broadening them, and prefer stronger gating/classification over always-on preprocessing.
12. Do not assume a larger pure-assignment threshold is automatically safer, and do not assume removed-clause ratio by itself fixes that problem. A follow-up sweep found that raising the gate to `>= 5` assignments looked clearly better on both the exact-CLI pure-hit slice (`0.4591s -> 0.4217s`) and the same-day exact-CLI mixed slice with the main hotspots (`22.5906s -> 22.1814s`), yet still lost the repeat-aware exact-CLI 59-case suite at `27.7944s`. A newer temporary gate that piggybacked on the same fixpoint and required both `>= 2` assignments and removed-clause ratio `>= 0.08` also looked good on the pure-hit slice (`0.5957s -> 0.5573s` against its local `0.00` baseline) and the same-day mixed slice (`26.0581s -> 25.4692s`), and even stayed positive on the stricter forward/reverse mixed A/B. But it still failed the real repeat-aware exact-CLI 59-case suite badly at `31.4387s`. So future root pure-literal tuning needs a classifier stronger than assignment count or removed-clause ratio alone, and slice-local exact-CLI wins are still not enough by themselves to justify changing the retained gate.
13. Do not add another whole-formula front-loaded purity pass just to decide whether to run the current root pure-literal presolve. A follow-up experiment found a seemingly perfect corpus predictor: every currently useful case with total root pure assignments `>= 2` already has at least two first-round pure literals, and all the one-pure cases stay at one. But turning that into an extra first-round screening pass still regressed the repeat-aware exact-CLI 59-case suite badly (`29.3678s`), even though the same-day mixed slice improved slightly (`23.4612s -> 23.3365s`). So future root-pure gating should avoid extra full normalization/polarity scans unless they remove much larger downstream work than this did.
14. Treat manual ternary-clause local unpack/write-back inside `propagate()` as another dead end unless a much stronger structural change comes with it. A scratch branch that manually unpacked ternary clauses into locals and wrote the watched order back explicitly still regressed the five-case hotspot slice in both orders (`29.6744s -> 31.0203s` forward, `28.7830s -> 30.9007s` reverse) while keeping identical conflict counts on every case, so shaving a few `lits[...]` reads by itself is not enough.
15. Treat one-pass normalized-clause reuse through root pure discovery and clause ingest as another weak startup cleanup, not a proven win. The scratch branch preserved exact hotspot conflict counts and was nearly tied on the serial five-case slice, but it still lost the real exact-CLI full suite slightly (`29.7802s -> 29.8429s`) while staying `59/59` correct. So future preprocessing/startup cleanup should demand a stronger suite-level signal than “remove one duplicate normalization pass.”
16. Treat fixed-order problem ternary clauses plus watched-position side arrays as another dead end unless a stronger simplification comes with them. An out-of-tree `OrientationSolver` kept exact conflict counts on every hotspot case and still regressed badly in both orders (`35.4075s -> 38.7377s` forward, `33.8519s -> 37.5611s` reverse), so replacing `clause.lits` mutation with extra watched-position state is not enough by itself.
17. Do not assume active problem-ternary watcher batches are already homogeneous, but also do not treat physical list separation by itself as the missing win. The profiler split still says batches containing problem ternary clauses are mixed `47.21%..70.78%` of the time on the main hotspots, with `0.96..2.36` non-problem co-resident watchers per batch on average, mostly learnt-large traffic. But the bounded scratch `SplitWatchSolver` that actually moved original problem-ternary clauses into dedicated watch lists still changed the search path badly enough to regress hard on `large/test_6.cnf` (`11.9614s` / `59,201` conflicts -> `16.9394s` / `81,161`) and `large/test_8.cnf` (`3.3173s` / `16,430` -> `9.2863s` / `44,287`), even though it helped `special/hard.cnf`. So future split-list work needs a much stronger semantics-preservation story than “the batches are mixed, therefore separate the lists,” and it still must stay clearly distinct from the already-rejected branch-hoist and clause-local-side-state directions.
18. Treat `satsolver_blaze.py` as a stale alternate-worker lead on the current hotspot family. A direct module-mode comparison now has the retained solver clearly ahead in both orders (`29.8179s` vs `35.5141s` forward, `35.8424s` vs `43.0727s` reverse), with blaze only stealing one forward `large/test_10.cnf` run. Future portfolio work needs a more materially different and current search identity than simply reviving the older sibling solver.
19. Use `tools/hotspot_compare.py` for future forward/reverse hotspot A/B checks before spending full-suite benchmark time on small solver changes. The tool already supports module-vs-module, module-vs-CLI, and CLI-vs-CLI comparisons with repeat-aware representative times and checker-backed validation, so it should replace the recent ad hoc shell snippets.
20. Treat `satsolver_fast.py` as a meaningful exact-CLI alternate candidate, not dead code and not yet the new mainline. The lean wrapper that removes root pure-literal presolve while keeping the current CDCL core, presolvers, and portfolio path beat the same-day exact-CLI 59-case single run `29.3963s -> 28.4781s` and landed `27.3829s` repeat-aware in `out_fast_cli_extended.txt`, both `59/59` correct. But it still did not beat the historical best exact-CLI snapshot for `satsolver.py` (`27.1974s`). So future exact-submission work should use `satsolver_fast.py` as the current alternate baseline, and any attempt to merge that win back into `satsolver.py` should target a smarter root-pure policy rather than just deleting the presolve blindly.
21. Do not remove the post-solve `model_satisfies(...)` self-check from `satsolver_fast.py` unless a future benchmark corpus makes that path materially larger. On the current benchmark set, the entire SAT-only check totals just `0.005311s` across all `28` SAT formulas, with the worst single case only `0.000713s`. A repeat-aware exact-CLI rerun of the no-self-check variant still landed at `27.6785s`, worse than the retained `satsolver_fast.py` snapshot `27.3829s`. So CLI-only safety removals of this size are not worth keeping.
22. Do not assume parser-integrated first-round-pure gating is enough to rescue root-pure preprocessing on `satsolver_fast.py`. Even after confirming that all current root-pure hit cases already have `first_round_pure_count >= 2`, a branch that collected those counts during DIMACS parsing and only then ran iterative root-pure preprocessing was still a near-tie at best: it regressed slightly on the exact-CLI root-hit slice (`0.4382s -> 0.4407s`) and was only effectively tied on the mixed exact-CLI slice (`24.6599s -> 24.6480s`). So future exact-CLI root-pure work still needs a materially stronger classifier or a broader win than this parser-gate branch showed.
23. Do not assume a standalone no-root-pure copy of the full solver is better than the current wrapper-style `satsolver_fast.py`. A branch that replaced the wrapper with a copied `satsolver.py` minus root-pure presolve regressed badly on the exact-CLI root-hit SAT slice (`0.4336s -> 0.4996s`) and was only slightly positive on the mixed nine-case hotspot slice (`24.4869s -> 24.4441s`). So future alternate exact-CLI files need to be materially smaller or more structurally different than a duplicated main solver, not just “the same code without root-pure.”
24. Do not assume a smaller wrapper around the same no-root-pure alternate core is enough to beat the retained `satsolver_fast.py`. A scratch min-wrapper that trimmed the current alternate file down further still lost the exact-CLI root-hit SAT slice on the two-order average (`0.4159s -> 0.4511s`) and then lost the repeat-aware exact-CLI 59-case suite overall (`27.3829s -> 27.5180s`), even though it improved the mixed nine-case hotspot slice (`24.8028s -> 24.5644s`). So future alternate exact-CLI file work needs a more meaningful semantic or code-size win than wrapper reshaping around the same no-root-pure solver core. The same cycle also measured full-corpus structural presolver cost directly: pigeonhole plus XOR checks totaled only about `0.0643s` across all 59 benchmark cases, so dropping those presolvers is unlikely to be the next useful exact-CLI lever either.
25. Do not assume a lazy-import alternate file with duplicated parser/output/structural presolvers is enough to beat the retained `satsolver_fast.py`. A scratch `scratch_satsolver_fast_lazy.py` did improve the six-case structural-hit exact-CLI slice (`0.1811s -> 0.1780s`), stayed slightly positive on the mixed nine-case hotspot slice (`24.7933s -> 24.7768s`), and even beat the retained alternate on a same-day exact-CLI single-run full suite (`27.1851s -> 26.9872s`). But it still lost the repeat-aware exact-CLI 59-case gate at `27.5546s`, worse than the retained `27.3829s`. So future alternate exact-CLI file work should not trust startup-sensitive slice wins or a one-off full-suite win by themselves; it still needs a stronger repeat-aware suite-level signal than “lazy-load the main solver behind duplicated structural presolvers.”
26. Do not drop the structural pigeonhole/XOR presolvers from future exact-CLI alternate files just because their aggregate corpus cost is small. A scratch lazy-core alternate that kept only local parse/output work and lazy-imported the solver core without those presolvers regressed the SAT-heavy root-hit slice (`0.4081s -> 0.4182s`) and catastrophically regressed the mixed exact-CLI hotspot slice (`24.3616s -> 32.2099s`) because `special/tseitin.cnf` alone blew up from about `0.03s` to about `7.43..7.46s`. So future alternate-file work should treat those structural shortcuts as required exact-CLI fast exits, not optional startup overhead.
27. Treat exact-CLI DIMACS parse/write overhead as a real but small lever on `satsolver_fast.py`. Replacing the inherited text parser/writer with a byte-level local `parse_dimacs[_file]()` plus byte-output path improved the same-day SAT-heavy root-hit exact-CLI slice (`0.4431s -> 0.4319s`) and improved the same-day repeat-aware exact-CLI 59-case comparison against the retained wrapper from `27.6459s` to `27.4523s`, both `59/59` correct. But the mixed nine-case hotspot slice was effectively tied (`24.6944s -> 24.6945s`), the refreshed merged artifact still landed at `27.5074s`, and the historical best retained `satsolver_fast.py` snapshot `27.3829s` remains unbeaten. So future alternate exact-CLI file work can revisit parser/read/write overhead, but it should treat gains here as sub-1% and noisy, require same-day repeat-aware baseline-vs-candidate measurements, and still keep the structural pigeonhole/XOR presolvers intact.
28. Do not assume the same byte-level DIMACS parse/write path that helped `satsolver_fast.py` will also help the main submission file `satsolver.py`. A main-solver branch using byte-level `parse_dimacs_file()` and byte-output `write_result()` improved the exact-CLI SAT-heavy root-hit slice (`0.4960s -> 0.4718s`) and was nearly tied on the mixed nine-case hotspot slice (`24.6647s -> 24.6994s`), but it still regressed the same-day repeat-aware exact-CLI 59-case suite badly (`27.6153s -> 29.3807s`), both `59/59` correct. So future parser/read/write work should stay on alternate exact-CLI wrappers unless a main-solver branch can clear the same-day repeat-aware full-suite gate; slice-local wins are not enough.
29. Treat lazy structural wrappers around `satsolver_fast.py` as another dead end unless the future design is materially different. A second-generation scratch wrapper with local byte-level parse/output, local structural pigeonhole/XOR fast exits, and lazy import of `satsolver_fast` still regressed the structural-hit slice (`0.1857s -> 0.1924s`), the SAT-heavy root-hit slice (`0.4189s -> 0.4208s`), and the mixed nine-case hotspot slice (`24.3005s -> 24.6247s`). So the “do local structural checks, then import the current alternate solver anyway” idea does not appear to recover the old lazy-import story after the bytes-parser keep.
30. Treat direct streamed-file DIMACS parsing in `satsolver_fast.py` as another dead end unless a future parser design removes materially more work than the current byte parser does. A scratch candidate that replaced the retained `read() + splitlines()` byte parser with a streaming binary-line loop regressed the first exact-CLI gate from `0.3701s` to `0.3931s` on the SAT-heavy root-hit slice (`0.3721s -> 0.3778s` forward, `0.3680s -> 0.4083s` reverse). So parse-path work on the alternate exact-CLI file now looks especially noise-sensitive and should demand a stronger same-day signal before earning broader benchmarking.
31. Treat “replace the narrow portfolio gate with one serial phase-biased worker” as another dead end. A branch that changed `satsolver_fast.py` so the current portfolio gate called `solve_cnf_serial(..., seed_phase_bias=True)` instead of the two-worker portfolio did produce a real exact-CLI `large/test_8.cnf` win (`0.2922s -> 0.2207s` two-order average), but it still lost the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice overall (`24.3702s -> 24.5513s`) because the reverse-order regressions outweighed the forward win. So future portfolio work still needs a broader suite-level story than just avoiding `fork()` on the one gated SAT-like family.
32. Treat broader learnt-database trimming aggressiveness as another dead end unless a future idea brings a materially better classifier than “same ranking, keep a smaller fraction.” A branch that changed `reduce_database()` to keep only the top `40%` of ranked candidates instead of the top `50%` blew up the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice from `24.6309s` to `40.4076s`, with `large/test_8.cnf` alone jumping from about `0.29s` to about `12.18s`. So future learnt-large watcher work should not try to solve the problem by simply trimming the ranked candidate pool harder across the board.
33. Treat parser-path work in `satsolver_fast.py` as another exhausted lane unless the future design changes much more than how the bytes are tokenized. A scratch manual byte-scanner parser regressed the first exact-CLI gate from `0.4605s` to `0.4908s` on the SAT-heavy root-hit slice, after the earlier streamed-line parser already lost `0.3701s -> 0.3931s`. So the retained bytes parser keep now looks like the end of the easy exact-CLI parser wins, not the start of a larger parser-optimization ladder.
34. Treat “same ranking, same keep fraction, reduce sooner” as another learnt-database dead end unless a future branch brings a materially better classifier than a smaller `next_reduce` multiplier. A branch that only changed the post-reduction schedule from `int(len(self.learnt_ids) * 1.5) + 64` to `int(len(self.learnt_ids) * 1.25) + 64` regressed the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice from `24.4791s` to `30.9079s`, with `large/test_8.cnf` alone jumping from about `0.29s` to about `2.32s` and the dense UNSAT cases also getting worse. So future learnt-large work should not assume that “reduce earlier” is a safer version of aggressive trimming.
35. Treat “same keep fraction, but prefer shorter learnt clauses before activity within the same LBD bucket” as another learnt-database dead end unless a future branch brings a much stronger classifier. A branch that changed the reduction sort from `(lbd, -activity, len)` to `(lbd, len, -activity)` regressed the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice from `24.9575s` to `30.6752s`, with `large/test_6.cnf` jumping from about `12.50s` to about `16.86s` on the two-order average and `large/test_8.cnf` tripling from about `0.28s` to about `0.91s`. So future learnt-large work should not assume that shorter-first tie-breaking is a safe way to attack watcher churn.
36. Treat narrow exact-CLI hybrids between `satsolver_fast.py` and `satsolver.py` as another dead end unless a future selector has a much stronger classifier than `num_vars`, density, and all-3-SAT shape. A scratch wrapper that kept `satsolver_fast.py` as the default path but routed formulas with `num_vars >= 250`, density `> 5.0`, and all clauses length `3` back to `satsolver.py` regressed the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice from `24.6659s` to `25.0305s`. The intended `large/test_6.cnf` rescue only appeared in one order, while `special/hard.cnf`, `large/test_10.cnf`, and small startup-sensitive cases gave the gain back. So future hybrid exact-CLI work should not assume that a one-band dense-3-SAT selector is enough.
37. Treat learnt-clause activity bumping as still essential to the current solver unless a future branch replaces its ranking signal with something materially better. A branch that removed `self.bump_clause_activity(current_clause_id)` from `analyze()` regressed the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice from `25.5245s` to `34.0354s`, with `large/test_6.cnf`, `special/hard.cnf`, and `large/test_8.cnf` all getting substantially worse. So future learnt-database work should not assume that clause activity is merely low-value bookkeeping because its direct runtime cost is modest.
38. Treat size-normalized learnt-clause activity as another dead end unless a future classifier changes more than the sort key. A branch that kept the same top-half retention and reduction schedule but ranked candidates by `(lbd, -(activity / len), len, -activity)` still regressed the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice from `25.3946s` to `30.0746s`, with the main damage again landing on `large/test_6.cnf` and `large/test_8.cnf`. So future learnt-database work should not assume that normalizing activity by clause length is a safe middle ground between the retained ranking and the already-rejected shorter-first tie-break.
39. Treat the promoted helper split as the new submission baseline. `satsolver.py` now uses the byte-parser/no-root-pure exact-CLI wrapper over `satsolver_core.py`, while still exporting the old core API (`Solver`, `Clause`, `solve_cnf_serial()`, root-pure helpers, portfolio helpers) for tests and tooling. That promotion beat the previous mainline on the same-day root-hit exact-CLI slice (`0.5026s -> 0.4044s`), the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice (`24.5923s -> 24.1644s`), and the same-day repeat-aware exact-CLI 59-case suite (`30.3078s -> 29.5746s`), all `59/59` correct. Future exact-CLI work should benchmark against this promoted wrapper, not the old monolithic main file.
40. Do not assume the sibling `satsolver_fast.py` is obsolete just because the wrapper path was promoted. On the same day, the promoted `satsolver.py` beat `satsolver_fast.py` on the root-hit slice (`0.4516s -> 0.4391s`) and on the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice (`25.2656s -> 24.5747s`), but `satsolver_fast.py` still landed a slightly better broad repeat-aware exact-CLI rerun (`29.1527s` vs promoted `29.5746s`). So future exact-CLI decisions should use same-day hotspot A/B plus same-day repeat-aware full-suite A/B together; neither sibling should be assumed dominant from one artifact alone.
41. Treat runtime-only import cleanup as a real but narrow exact-CLI lever on the promoted wrapper baseline. Removing runtime `typing` imports from `satsolver.py`, `satsolver_fast.py`, and `satsolver_core.py` improved the 12-case SAT-heavy root-hit slice (`0.4338s -> 0.3878s`), the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice (`24.5782s -> 24.4033s`), and the same-day repeat-aware exact-CLI 59-case suite (`28.3088s -> 27.9510s`), all still correct. But the broad gain is only about `1.26%`, so future startup-path work should target similarly heavy imports or wrapper/module overhead and still require same-day repeat-aware 59-case confirmation; import-time traces and startup-sensitive slices alone are not enough.
42. Do not assume the remaining top-level wrapper/core imports are another free exact-CLI win after the `typing` cleanup. A follow-on branch that removed the remaining top-level `os`/`sys` imports from `satsolver_core.py` and moved them into the few functions that actually use them, while also moving `sys` into `main()` in `satsolver.py` and `satsolver_fast.py`, did improve the 12-case SAT-heavy root-hit slice (`0.4387s -> 0.4052s`) but still regressed the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice from `23.9617s` to `24.2357s`. So future startup-path work should treat the kept `typing` cleanup as the useful stopping point for this lane unless a new idea can show a broader solver-path win than import trimming alone.
43. Treat “drop the wrapper's unused export ballast” as another exact-CLI startup dead end unless a future alternate-file idea changes substantially more than alias surface area. A scratch `scratch_satsolver_leanfast.py` wrapper that kept the same byte parser, structural presolvers, and solve path but omitted most of the broad exported alias surface still lost the 12-case SAT-heavy root-hit exact-CLI gate on the two-order average (`0.3571s -> 0.3623s`). Reintroducing only the hot internal aliases also still lost (`0.3474s -> 0.3530s`) and made the import-time smoke check worse. So future alternate-file startup work should not assume that reducing exported wrapper names is a meaningful lever by itself.
44. Treat tokenized locked-clause marks in `reduce_database()` as another learnt-database micro-optimization dead end unless a future branch changes more than one small allocation site. A branch that replaced the per-reduction Python `set` of locked clause IDs with reusable `clause_marks` / `clause_mark_token` state still regressed the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice from `24.9111s` to `25.8251s`. The forward order was slightly positive (`25.1938s -> 24.9983s`), but the reverse order lost badly (`24.6283s -> 26.6520s`), with the biggest damage on `large/test_6.cnf`. So future `reduce_database()` bookkeeping work should not assume that replacing a small `set` allocation with mark arrays is automatically an end-to-end win.
45. Treat parse-time structural-summary collection as another exact-CLI startup dead end unless a future parser design makes the summary work materially cheaper than the current standalone scans. A scratch `scratch_satsolver_statsfast.py` wrapper that collected pigeonhole, XOR, and portfolio summaries incrementally during parsing regressed the 12-case SAT-heavy exact-CLI root-hit slice from `0.3818s` to `0.4267s` on the two-order average. So future alternate exact-CLI work should not assume that folding structural presolve checks into parsing is a free win; a heavier parser can easily cost more than the rescans it removes.
46. Treat lazy export forwarding in `satsolver.py` as another exact-CLI startup dead end unless a future wrapper design removes more than top-level alias binding. A branch that replaced the main wrapper's broad alias block with module `__getattr__` forwarding and patch-friendly `globals().get(..., base....)` fallbacks did barely improve the 12-case SAT-heavy root-hit slice (`0.3592s -> 0.3524s`) but still regressed the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice from `24.1326s` to `24.4102s`, with the biggest reverse-order damage on `special/hard.cnf`. So future `satsolver.py` startup work should not assume that delaying export resolution is enough to produce a net submission-path win.
47. Treat direct SAT-output byte emission as another exact-CLI startup dead end unless a future wrapper design removes substantially more work than `format_model(...).encode("ascii")` alone. A scratch alternate that changed only `write_result()` in `satsolver_fast.py`-style code to build the SAT model line directly with a `bytearray` still regressed the 12-case SAT-heavy exact-CLI root-hit slice from `0.3717s` to `0.3843s` on the two-order average. Combined with the earlier `large/test_8.cnf` profile, which showed output formatting to be tiny next to parse/read and portfolio overhead, this says future submission-path work should stay focused on broader parse/import/solve-path reductions rather than isolated SAT line formatting.
48. Treat tiny immutable clause-shape metadata as a still-live propagation lane, but keep the boundary tight. A core branch that added `Clause.ternary` and used it instead of `len(lits) == 3` in `propagate()` improved the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice from `25.9133s` to `25.0078s` and improved the same-day repeat-aware exact-CLI 59-case baseline-vs-candidate comparison from `29.1167s` to `28.3019s`, with the refreshed retained artifact landing at `27.8701s`, all `59/59` correct. But the SAT-heavy root-hit slice was slightly worse (`0.3694s -> 0.3722s`), and the earlier `Clause.size` / mutable side-array experiments still lost. So future propagation work can consider similarly cheap immutable family flags, but should not treat this as permission to resurrect broader duplicated clause metadata or mutable watch-position state.
49. Do not assume every reuse of immutable clause-shape metadata is a free win outside `propagate()`. A scratch branch that reused `Clause.ternary` inside `minimize_learnt()` and removed the local `len(reason_lits)` shape test looked excellent on the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice (`24.7815s -> 23.3213s`), but it still regressed the 12-case SAT-heavy root-hit slice (`0.3652s -> 0.3889s`) and the repeat-aware exact-CLI 59-case suite (`26.5996s -> 27.9836s`), with `large/test_6.cnf` worsening from `11.5792s` to `13.0787s`. So future immutable metadata work should keep the same full-suite caution as other small conflict-analysis fast paths; a hotspot win inside `minimize_learnt()` is not enough by itself.
50. Treat hand-unrolled fixed-size reason branches beyond ternary as another likely `minimize_learnt()` dead end unless a future variant shows a much stronger full-slice signal. A scratch exact 4-literal reason fast path regressed the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice from `23.9068s` to `24.9093s`, mainly because `special/hard.cnf` worsened from `8.1569s` to `10.1933s` while `large/test_6.cnf` improved only modestly (`11.7708s -> 11.5467s`). So future conflict-analysis specialization should be skeptical of extending the current binary/ternary one-hop unroll pattern to larger fixed reason sizes.
51. Treat schedule-only learnt-database changes as another dead end unless a future branch introduces a materially better classifier than just changing the post-reduction multiplier. A scratch branch that raised the post-reduction `next_reduce` growth factor from `1.5` to `1.75` regressed the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice from `23.5526s` to `33.5169s`, with catastrophic damage on `large/test_8.cnf` (`0.2912s -> 6.6520s` forward, `0.2766s -> 6.4384s` reverse) and heavy losses on `large/test_6.cnf` too (`11.5209s -> 15.2828s` forward, `11.3521s -> 15.4253s` reverse). So both “reduce earlier” and “reduce later” are now clearly unsafe without a better learnt-clause retention/reduction classifier.
52. Treat fixed-size watched-clause specialization beyond ternary as another likely propagation dead end unless a future branch shows a materially stronger broad exact-CLI win than the quaternary attempt did. A scratch branch that added `Clause.quaternary` plus a dedicated exact-4-literal watched-clause path in `propagate()` did improve the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice (`23.8342s -> 23.6216s`), but it still regressed the 12-case SAT-heavy root-hit slice (`0.3453s -> 0.3528s`) and the repeat-aware exact-CLI 59-case suite (`26.8303s -> 27.4920s`), with the broad damage concentrated on `large/test_6.cnf`, `medium/test_4.cnf`, and `large/test_10.cnf`. So future immutable family-flag work should not assume the next fixed watched size after ternary is worth specializing by default.
53. Treat tiny `append()` / `pop()` lookup cleanup inside `propagate()` as another likely micro-optimization dead end unless a future branch removes more structural work than just rebinding hot list methods. A scratch branch that localized `trail.append` and per-watcher-list `watchers.pop` inside `propagate()` looked positive in forward order (`25.1835s -> 24.5555s`) but still regressed the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice on the two-order average (`24.1557s -> 24.2120s`). The persistent losses on `large/test_6.cnf` and `special/hard.cnf` outweighed the unstable forward-order wins on `medium/test_3.cnf` and `medium/test_4.cnf`. So future propagation work should not assume that raw list-method lookup cost can be harvested cleanly without removing more real watcher/trail churn too.
54. Treat explicit CLI-mode/import-mode separation as a still-live wrapper lane, unlike lazy export forwarding or blanket alias trimming. A scratch import-gated `satsolver.py` that only builds the broad alias/test surface when imported, while using `satsolver_core` symbols directly on the CLI path, improved the 12-case SAT-heavy root-hit exact-CLI slice (`0.3905s -> 0.3842s`), the mixed nine-case exact-CLI hotspot slice (`25.2601s -> 23.5388s`), and the same-day repeat-aware exact-CLI baseline-vs-candidate suite (`27.6064s -> 27.5425s`), with the refreshed retained artifact landing at `26.4762s`. Future startup work should prefer this explicit “lean when run as a script, rich when imported” split over lazy export forwarding or alias-surface trimming, but it should still demand same-day repeat-aware full-suite confirmation because the broad A/B margin was modest.
55. So future phase work should keep treating phase-bias seeding as a narrow specialist heuristic rather than a broad default-policy improvement.
94. Treat portfolio-worker wrapper churn as another nearly-exhausted one-case lane unless a future branch brings a materially stronger `large/test_8.cnf` win than this. A scratch branch that kept the current narrow portfolio gate but switched both workers from `solve_cnf_serial()` to `solve_cnf_fast_serial()` still regressed the repeat-2 exact-CLI `large/test_8.cnf` two-order average from `0.2924s` to `0.2950s` (`0.2772s -> 0.3008s` forward, `0.3075s -> 0.2892s` reverse). So future portfolio work should demand a clearly positive one-case exact-CLI signal before spending more mixed-slice or full-suite benchmarking budget on worker-plumbing tweaks.
``````

Raw content:

``````python
from __future__ import annotations

import sys

import satsolver_core as base

CLI_MODE = __name__ == "__main__"

if CLI_MODE:
    Solver = base.Solver
    model_satisfies = base.model_satisfies
    has_pigeonhole_core = base.has_pigeonhole_core
    xor_system_unsat = base.xor_system_unsat
    format_model = base.format_model
    should_use_parallel_portfolio = base.should_use_parallel_portfolio
else:
    import os

    TRUE = base.TRUE
    FALSE = base.FALSE
    UNASSIGNED = base.UNASSIGNED

    PORTFOLIO_DISABLE_ENV = base.PORTFOLIO_DISABLE_ENV
    PORTFOLIO_MIN_VARS = base.PORTFOLIO_MIN_VARS
    PORTFOLIO_MIN_CLAUSES = base.PORTFOLIO_MIN_CLAUSES
    PORTFOLIO_MAX_DENSITY = base.PORTFOLIO_MAX_DENSITY
    ROOT_PURE_LITERAL_MIN_ASSIGNMENTS = base.ROOT_PURE_LITERAL_MIN_ASSIGNMENTS

    luby = base.luby
    lit_index = base.lit_index
    normalize_clause_literals = base.normalize_clause_literals
    find_iterative_root_pure_literals = base.find_iterative_root_pure_literals
    Clause = base.Clause
    Solver = base.Solver
    model_satisfies = base.model_satisfies
    has_pigeonhole_core = base.has_pigeonhole_core
    xor_system_unsat = base.xor_system_unsat
    format_model = base.format_model


def parse_dimacs_bytes(data: bytes) -> tuple[int, list[list[int]]]:
    num_vars: int | None = None
    num_clauses: int | None = None
    clauses: list[list[int]] = []
    current: list[int] = []
    header_seen = False

    for raw_line in data.splitlines():
        line = raw_line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith(b"c"):
            continue
        if line.startswith(b"%"):
            break
        if line.startswith(b"p"):
            if header_seen:
                raise ValueError("Multiple DIMACS problem lines are not allowed")
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) != 4 or parts[1] != b"cnf":
                raise ValueError("Invalid DIMACS problem line")
            num_vars = int(parts[2])
            num_clauses = int(parts[3])
            header_seen = True
            continue
        if not header_seen:
            raise ValueError("DIMACS clauses must appear after the problem line")

        for token in line.split():
            literal = int(token)
            if literal == 0:
                clauses.append(current)
                current = []
            else:
                if abs(literal) > num_vars:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Literal {literal} exceeds declared variable range 1..{num_vars}"
                    )
                current.append(literal)

    if num_vars is None or num_clauses is None:
        raise ValueError("Missing DIMACS problem line")
    if current:
        raise ValueError("Last clause is missing its terminating 0")
    if len(clauses) != num_clauses:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Clause count mismatch: header says {num_clauses}, parsed {len(clauses)}"
        )

    return num_vars, clauses


def parse_dimacs(text: str) -> tuple[int, list[list[int]]]:
    return parse_dimacs_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))


def parse_dimacs_file(path: str) -> tuple[int, list[list[int]]]:
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        return parse_dimacs_bytes(handle.read())

if not CLI_MODE:

    def solve_cnf_serial(
        num_vars: int,
        clauses: list[list[int]],
        *,
        seed_phase_bias: bool = False,
    ) -> list[int] | None:
        solver = Solver(num_vars)
        root_pure_literals = base.find_iterative_root_pure_literals(num_vars, clauses)
        if len(root_pure_literals) >= base.ROOT_PURE_LITERAL_MIN_ASSIGNMENTS:
            for literal in root_pure_literals:
                if not solver.enqueue(literal, None):
                    return None
        for clause in clauses:
            if not solver.add_problem_clause(clause):
                return None
        if seed_phase_bias:
            solver.seed_saved_phases_from_bias()
        return solver.solve()


def solve_cnf_fast_serial(
    num_vars: int,
    clauses: list[list[int]],
    *,
    seed_phase_bias: bool = False,
) -> list[int] | None:
    solver = Solver(num_vars)
    for clause in clauses:
        if not solver.add_problem_clause(clause):
            return None
    if seed_phase_bias:
        solver.seed_saved_phases_from_bias()
    return solver.solve()


if not CLI_MODE:

    def should_use_parallel_portfolio(num_vars: int, clauses: list[list[int]]) -> bool:
        return base.should_use_parallel_portfolio(num_vars, clauses)


def solve_cnf_portfolio(num_vars: int, clauses: list[list[int]]) -> list[int] | None:
    import multiprocessing as mp

    def solve_portfolio_worker(seed_phase_bias: bool, result_queue) -> None:
        try:
            model = solve_cnf_fast_serial(num_vars, clauses, seed_phase_bias=seed_phase_bias)
            result_queue.put((True, model))
        except BaseException as exc:
            result_queue.put((False, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"))

    context = mp.get_context("fork")
    result_queue = context.Queue()
    processes = [
        context.Process(target=solve_portfolio_worker, args=(False, result_queue)),
        context.Process(target=solve_portfolio_worker, args=(True, result_queue)),
    ]

    for process in processes:
        process.start()

    errors: list[str] = []

    try:
        remaining = len(processes)
        while remaining > 0:
            ok, payload = result_queue.get()
            remaining -= 1
            if ok:
                return payload
            errors.append(payload)
    finally:
        for process in processes:
            if process.is_alive():
                process.terminate()
        for process in processes:
            process.join()
        result_queue.close()
        result_queue.join_thread()

    raise RuntimeError(f"Parallel portfolio failed: {'; '.join(errors)}")


def solve_cnf(num_vars: int, clauses: list[list[int]]) -> list[int] | None:
    if has_pigeonhole_core(clauses):
        return None
    if xor_system_unsat(num_vars, clauses):
        return None
    if should_use_parallel_portfolio(num_vars, clauses):
        return solve_cnf_portfolio(num_vars, clauses)
    return solve_cnf_fast_serial(num_vars, clauses)


def write_result(path: str, model: list[int] | None) -> None:
    with open(path, "wb") as handle:
        if model is None:
            handle.write(b"UNSAT\n")
        else:
            handle.write(b"SAT\n")
            handle.write(format_model(model).encode("ascii"))
            handle.write(b"\n")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    arguments = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    if len(arguments) != 2:
        print("Usage: python satsolver.py input.cnf output.txt", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    input_path, output_path = arguments
    try:
        num_vars, clauses = parse_dimacs_file(input_path)
        model = solve_cnf(num_vars, clauses)
        if model is not None and not model_satisfies(clauses, model):
            raise RuntimeError("Internal error: produced model does not satisfy the input CNF")
        write_result(output_path, model)
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - CLI safety path
        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
``````

### `satsolver_blaze.py`

- Category: Core runtime / benchmark code
- Git status: tracked
- Size: `23818` bytes
- Line count: `731`
- Why it matters: Older alternate wrapper/solver variant retained for comparison.

Raw content:

``````python
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Iterable, Optional


TRUE = 1
FALSE = -1
UNASSIGNED = 0


def luby(index: int) -> int:
    """Return the 1-indexed Luby sequence value."""
    if index < 1:
        raise ValueError("Luby sequence is 1-indexed")

    size = 1
    while size < index + 1:
        size = 2 * size + 1
    while size - 1 != index:
        size = (size - 1) // 2
        index %= size
    return (size + 1) // 2


def lit_index(literal: int) -> int:
    variable = abs(literal)
    return variable * 2 if literal > 0 else variable * 2 + 1


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Clause:
    lits: list[int]
    learnt: bool = False
    activity: float = 0.0
    lbd: int = 0
    deleted: bool = False


class Solver:
    """A compact CDCL solver with watched literals, VSIDS-style activity, and restarts."""

    def __init__(self, num_vars: int) -> None:
        self.num_vars = num_vars
        self.clauses: list[Clause] = []
        self.learnt_ids: list[int] = []
        self.binary_implications: list[list[tuple[int, int]]] = [[] for _ in range(2 * num_vars + 2)]
        self.watchers: list[list[int]] = [[] for _ in range(2 * num_vars + 2)]

        self.values = [UNASSIGNED] * (num_vars + 1)
        self.level = [0] * (num_vars + 1)
        self.reason: list[Optional[int]] = [None] * (num_vars + 1)

        self.activity = [0.0] * (num_vars + 1)
        self.phase_bias = [0] * (num_vars + 1)
        self.saved_phase = [True] * (num_vars + 1)
        self.var_inc = 1.0
        self.var_decay = 0.95
        self.clause_inc = 1.0
        self.clause_decay = 0.999

        self.trail: list[int] = []
        self.trail_limits: list[int] = []
        self.qhead = 0

        self.seen = [0] * (num_vars + 1)
        self.seen_token = 0
        self.lbd_marks = [0] * (num_vars + 1)
        self.lbd_token = 0

        self.conflicts = 0
        self.restart_base = 64
        self.next_reduce = 256

        self.ok = True

    def current_level(self) -> int:
        return len(self.trail_limits)

    def literal_value(self, literal: int) -> int:
        value = self.values[abs(literal)]
        if value == UNASSIGNED:
            return UNASSIGNED
        return value if literal > 0 else -value

    def enqueue(self, literal: int, reason: Optional[int]) -> bool:
        variable = abs(literal)
        value = TRUE if literal > 0 else FALSE
        current = self.values[variable]
        if current != UNASSIGNED:
            return current == value

        self.values[variable] = value
        self.level[variable] = self.current_level()
        self.reason[variable] = reason
        self.saved_phase[variable] = literal > 0
        self.trail.append(literal)
        return True

    def backtrack(self, level: int) -> None:
        while self.current_level() > level:
            start = self.trail_limits.pop()
            while len(self.trail) > start:
                literal = self.trail.pop()
                variable = abs(literal)
                self.values[variable] = UNASSIGNED
                self.level[variable] = 0
                self.reason[variable] = None
        self.qhead = len(self.trail)

    def attach_clause(self, clause_id: int) -> None:
        clause = self.clauses[clause_id]
        if len(clause.lits) == 2:
            first, second = clause.lits
            self.binary_implications[lit_index(-first)].append((second, clause_id))
            self.binary_implications[lit_index(-second)].append((first, clause_id))
            return
        self.watchers[lit_index(clause.lits[0])].append(clause_id)
        self.watchers[lit_index(clause.lits[1])].append(clause_id)

    def bump_var_activity(self, variable: int) -> None:
        self.activity[variable] += self.var_inc
        if self.activity[variable] > 1e100:
            for index in range(1, self.num_vars + 1):
                self.activity[index] *= 1e-100
            self.var_inc *= 1e-100

    def decay_var_activity(self) -> None:
        self.var_inc /= self.var_decay

    def bump_clause_activity(self, clause_id: int) -> None:
        clause = self.clauses[clause_id]
        clause.activity += self.clause_inc
        if clause.activity > 1e20:
            for learnt_id in self.learnt_ids:
                learnt = self.clauses[learnt_id]
                if not learnt.deleted:
                    learnt.activity *= 1e-20
            self.clause_inc *= 1e-20

    def decay_clause_activity(self) -> None:
        self.clause_inc /= self.clause_decay

    def observe_clause(self, literals: Iterable[int]) -> None:
        for literal in literals:
            variable = abs(literal)
            self.activity[variable] += 1.0
            self.phase_bias[variable] += 1 if literal > 0 else -1

    def normalize_clause(self, literals: Iterable[int]) -> Optional[list[int]]:
        clause: list[int] = []
        seen: set[int] = set()
        for literal in literals:
            if literal == 0:
                continue
            if -literal in seen:
                return None
            if literal not in seen:
                seen.add(literal)
                clause.append(literal)
        return clause

    def simplify_root_clause(self, literals: Iterable[int]) -> Optional[list[int]]:
        reduced: list[int] = []
        for literal in literals:
            value = self.literal_value(literal)
            if value == TRUE:
                return None
            if value != FALSE:
                reduced.append(literal)
        return reduced

    def add_problem_clause(self, literals: Iterable[int]) -> bool:
        if not self.ok:
            return False

        normalized = self.normalize_clause(literals)
        if normalized is None:
            return True

        self.observe_clause(normalized)
        reduced = self.simplify_root_clause(normalized)
        if reduced is None:
            return True
        if not reduced:
            self.ok = False
            return False

        clause_id = len(self.clauses)
        clause = Clause(reduced, learnt=False, lbd=0)
        self.clauses.append(clause)

        if len(reduced) == 1:
            if not self.enqueue(reduced[0], clause_id):
                self.ok = False
                return False
            conflict = self.propagate()
            if conflict is not None:
                self.ok = False
                return False
            return True

        self.attach_clause(clause_id)
        return True

    def add_learnt_clause(self, literals: list[int], lbd: int) -> int:
        clause_id = len(self.clauses)
        clause = Clause(list(literals), learnt=True, activity=self.clause_inc, lbd=lbd)
        self.clauses.append(clause)
        self.learnt_ids.append(clause_id)
        if len(literals) > 1:
            self.attach_clause(clause_id)
        return clause_id

    def propagate(self) -> Optional[int]:
        values = self.values
        binary_implications = self.binary_implications
        all_watchers = self.watchers

        while self.qhead < len(self.trail):
            literal = self.trail[self.qhead]
            self.qhead += 1

            for implied_literal, clause_id in binary_implications[lit_index(literal)]:
                clause = self.clauses[clause_id]
                if clause.deleted:
                    continue

                implied_value = values[abs(implied_literal)]
                if implied_literal < 0:
                    implied_value = -implied_value
                if implied_value == FALSE:
                    return clause_id
                if implied_value == UNASSIGNED and not self.enqueue(implied_literal, clause_id):
                    return clause_id

            false_literal = -literal
            watchers = all_watchers[lit_index(false_literal)]
            index = 0

            while index < len(watchers):
                clause_id = watchers[index]
                clause = self.clauses[clause_id]

                if clause.deleted:
                    watchers[index] = watchers[-1]
                    watchers.pop()
                    continue

                lits = clause.lits
                if lits[0] == false_literal:
                    lits[0], lits[1] = lits[1], lits[0]

                other_literal = lits[0]
                other_value = values[abs(other_literal)]
                if other_literal < 0:
                    other_value = -other_value

                if other_value == TRUE:
                    index += 1
                    continue

                found_replacement = False
                for replacement in range(2, len(lits)):
                    candidate_literal = lits[replacement]
                    candidate_value = values[abs(candidate_literal)]
                    if candidate_literal < 0:
                        candidate_value = -candidate_value
                    if candidate_value != FALSE:
                        lits[1], lits[replacement] = lits[replacement], lits[1]
                        all_watchers[lit_index(lits[1])].append(clause_id)
                        watchers[index] = watchers[-1]
                        watchers.pop()
                        found_replacement = True
                        break

                if found_replacement:
                    continue

                if other_value == FALSE:
                    return clause_id
                if other_value == UNASSIGNED and not self.enqueue(lits[0], clause_id):
                    return clause_id
                index += 1

        return None

    def compute_lbd(self, literals: Iterable[int]) -> int:
        self.lbd_token += 1
        token = self.lbd_token
        marks = self.lbd_marks
        levels = self.level
        count = 0

        for literal in literals:
            decision_level = levels[abs(literal)]
            if marks[decision_level] != token:
                marks[decision_level] = token
                count += 1

        return count

    def minimize_learnt(self, learnt: list[int], token: int) -> list[int]:
        if len(learnt) <= 2:
            return learnt

        minimized = [learnt[0]]
        levels = self.level
        reasons = self.reason
        seen = self.seen

        for literal in learnt[1:]:
            reason_clause_id = reasons[abs(literal)]
            if reason_clause_id is None:
                minimized.append(literal)
                continue

            redundant = True
            for reason_literal in self.clauses[reason_clause_id].lits:
                if reason_literal == -literal:
                    continue
                variable = abs(reason_literal)
                if levels[variable] != 0 and seen[variable] != token:
                    redundant = False
                    break

            if not redundant:
                minimized.append(literal)

        return minimized

    def analyze(self, conflict_clause_id: int) -> tuple[list[int], int, int]:
        learnt = [0]
        self.seen_token += 1
        token = self.seen_token
        touched: list[int] = []

        clauses = self.clauses
        levels = self.level
        reasons = self.reason
        seen = self.seen
        trail = self.trail
        current_level = self.current_level()

        current_clause_id = conflict_clause_id
        path_count = 0
        pivot = 0
        trail_index = len(trail) - 1

        while True:
            clause = clauses[current_clause_id]
            if clause.learnt:
                self.bump_clause_activity(current_clause_id)

            for literal in clause.lits:
                if literal == pivot:
                    continue
                variable = abs(literal)
                if seen[variable] == token or levels[variable] == 0:
                    continue

                seen[variable] = token
                touched.append(variable)
                self.bump_var_activity(variable)

                if levels[variable] == current_level:
                    path_count += 1
                else:
                    learnt.append(literal)

            while True:
                pivot = trail[trail_index]
                trail_index -= 1
                if seen[abs(pivot)] == token:
                    break

            seen[abs(pivot)] = 0
            path_count -= 1
            if path_count == 0:
                learnt[0] = -pivot
                break

            reason_clause_id = reasons[abs(pivot)]
            if reason_clause_id is None:
                learnt[0] = -pivot
                break
            current_clause_id = reason_clause_id

        learnt = self.minimize_learnt(learnt, token)

        for variable in touched:
            seen[variable] = 0

        if len(learnt) == 1:
            return learnt, 0, 1

        best_index = 1
        best_level = levels[abs(learnt[1])]
        for index in range(2, len(learnt)):
            variable_level = levels[abs(learnt[index])]
            if variable_level > best_level:
                best_level = variable_level
                best_index = index

        learnt[1], learnt[best_index] = learnt[best_index], learnt[1]
        return learnt, best_level, self.compute_lbd(learnt)

    def pick_branch_literal(self) -> int:
        best_variable = 0
        best_activity = -1.0
        for variable in range(1, self.num_vars + 1):
            if self.values[variable] == UNASSIGNED and self.activity[variable] > best_activity:
                best_activity = self.activity[variable]
                best_variable = variable

        if best_variable == 0:
            return 0

        positive = self.saved_phase[best_variable]
        if self.activity[best_variable] == 0.0:
            positive = self.phase_bias[best_variable] >= 0
        return best_variable if positive else -best_variable

    def reduce_database(self) -> None:
        if len(self.learnt_ids) < self.next_reduce:
            return

        locked = {clause_id for clause_id in self.reason[1:] if clause_id is not None}
        keep: list[int] = []
        candidates: list[int] = []

        for clause_id in self.learnt_ids:
            clause = self.clauses[clause_id]
            if clause.deleted:
                continue
            if clause_id in locked or len(clause.lits) <= 2 or clause.lbd <= 2:
                keep.append(clause_id)
            else:
                candidates.append(clause_id)

        candidates.sort(
            key=lambda clause_id: (
                self.clauses[clause_id].lbd,
                -self.clauses[clause_id].activity,
                len(self.clauses[clause_id].lits),
            )
        )
        midpoint = len(candidates) // 2
        keep.extend(candidates[:midpoint])
        for clause_id in candidates[midpoint:]:
            self.clauses[clause_id].deleted = True

        self.learnt_ids = keep
        self.next_reduce = max(256, int(len(self.learnt_ids) * 1.5) + 64)

    def build_model(self) -> list[int]:
        model = [FALSE] * (self.num_vars + 1)
        for variable in range(1, self.num_vars + 1):
            value = self.values[variable]
            if value == UNASSIGNED:
                value = TRUE if self.saved_phase[variable] else FALSE
            model[variable] = value
        return model

    def solve(self) -> Optional[list[int]]:
        if not self.ok:
            return None

        root_conflict = self.propagate()
        if root_conflict is not None:
            self.ok = False
            return None

        restart_index = 1
        conflicts_since_restart = 0
        restart_limit = self.restart_base * luby(restart_index)

        while True:
            conflict = self.propagate()
            if conflict is not None:
                self.conflicts += 1
                conflicts_since_restart += 1

                if self.current_level() == 0:
                    self.ok = False
                    return None

                learnt, backtrack_level, lbd = self.analyze(conflict)
                self.backtrack(backtrack_level)
                learnt_clause_id = self.add_learnt_clause(learnt, lbd)
                if not self.enqueue(learnt[0], learnt_clause_id):
                    self.ok = False
                    return None

                self.decay_var_activity()
                self.decay_clause_activity()

                if conflicts_since_restart >= restart_limit:
                    self.backtrack(0)
                    conflicts_since_restart = 0
                    restart_index += 1
                    restart_limit = self.restart_base * luby(restart_index)

                self.reduce_database()
                continue

            branch_literal = self.pick_branch_literal()
            if branch_literal == 0:
                return self.build_model()

            self.trail_limits.append(len(self.trail))
            self.enqueue(branch_literal, None)


def parse_dimacs(text: str) -> tuple[int, list[list[int]]]:
    num_vars: Optional[int] = None
    num_clauses: Optional[int] = None
    clauses: list[list[int]] = []
    current: list[int] = []

    for raw_line in text.splitlines():
        line = raw_line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("c"):
            continue
        if line.startswith("%"):
            break
        if line.startswith("p"):
            parts = line.split()
            if len(parts) != 4 or parts[1] != "cnf":
                raise ValueError("Invalid DIMACS problem line")
            num_vars = int(parts[2])
            num_clauses = int(parts[3])
            continue

        for token in line.split():
            literal = int(token)
            if literal == 0:
                clauses.append(current)
                current = []
            else:
                current.append(literal)

    if num_vars is None or num_clauses is None:
        raise ValueError("Missing DIMACS problem line")
    if current:
        raise ValueError("Last clause is missing its terminating 0")
    if len(clauses) != num_clauses:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Clause count mismatch: header says {num_clauses}, parsed {len(clauses)}"
        )

    return num_vars, clauses


def parse_dimacs_file(path: str) -> tuple[int, list[list[int]]]:
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return parse_dimacs(handle.read())


def model_satisfies(clauses: Iterable[Iterable[int]], model: list[int]) -> bool:
    for clause in clauses:
        if not any(model[abs(literal)] == (TRUE if literal > 0 else FALSE) for literal in clause):
            return False
    return True


def has_pigeonhole_core(clauses: Iterable[Iterable[int]]) -> bool:
    negative_pairs: set[tuple[int, int]] = set()
    positive_rows_by_width: dict[int, list[tuple[int, ...]]] = {}

    for clause in clauses:
        lits = list(clause)
        if len(lits) == 2 and lits[0] < 0 and lits[1] < 0:
            first, second = sorted((-lits[0], -lits[1]))
            negative_pairs.add((first, second))
        elif len(lits) > 1 and all(literal > 0 for literal in lits):
            row = tuple(sorted(dict.fromkeys(lits)))
            if len(row) == len(lits):
                positive_rows_by_width.setdefault(len(row), []).append(row)

    for width, rows in positive_rows_by_width.items():
        if len(rows) <= width:
            continue

        rows = sorted(rows)
        selected: list[tuple[int, ...]] = []
        used: set[int] = set()

        for row in rows:
            if used.isdisjoint(row):
                selected.append(row)
                used.update(row)

        if len(selected) <= width:
            continue

        core_found = True
        for column in range(width):
            column_vars = [row[column] for row in selected]
            for first_index in range(len(column_vars)):
                for second_index in range(first_index + 1, len(column_vars)):
                    pair = tuple(sorted((column_vars[first_index], column_vars[second_index])))
                    if pair not in negative_pairs:
                        core_found = False
                        break
                if not core_found:
                    break
            if not core_found:
                break

        if core_found:
            return True

    return False


def xor_system_unsat(num_vars: int, clauses: Iterable[Iterable[int]]) -> bool:
    groups: dict[tuple[int, ...], set[int]] = {}

    for clause in clauses:
        literals = list(clause)
        if len(literals) < 3 or len(literals) > 6:
            continue

        signs: dict[int, int] = {}
        valid = True
        for literal in literals:
            variable = abs(literal)
            if variable in signs:
                valid = False
                break
            signs[variable] = 1 if literal < 0 else 0

        if not valid:
            continue

        variables = tuple(sorted(signs))
        pattern = 0
        for index, variable in enumerate(variables):
            pattern |= signs[variable] << index
        groups.setdefault(variables, set()).add(pattern)

    basis: dict[int, tuple[int, int]] = {}
    equations: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

    for variables, patterns in groups.items():
        width = len(variables)
        if len(patterns) != (1 << (width - 1)):
            continue

        parities = {pattern.bit_count() & 1 for pattern in patterns}
        if len(parities) != 1:
            continue

        forbidden_parity = next(iter(parities))
        rhs = forbidden_parity ^ 1
        mask = 0
        for variable in variables:
            mask |= 1 << (variable - 1)
        equations.append((mask, rhs))

    for mask, rhs in equations:
        current_mask = mask
        current_rhs = rhs

        while current_mask:
            pivot = current_mask.bit_length() - 1
            row = basis.get(pivot)
            if row is None:
                basis[pivot] = (current_mask, current_rhs)
                break
            current_mask ^= row[0]
            current_rhs ^= row[1]
        else:
            if current_rhs:
                return True

    return False


def format_model(model: list[int]) -> str:
    literals = [str(variable if model[variable] == TRUE else -variable) for variable in range(1, len(model))]
    return " ".join(literals) + " 0"


def solve_cnf(num_vars: int, clauses: list[list[int]]) -> Optional[list[int]]:
    if has_pigeonhole_core(clauses):
        return None
    if xor_system_unsat(num_vars, clauses):
        return None

    solver = Solver(num_vars)
    for clause in clauses:
        if not solver.add_problem_clause(clause):
            return None
    return solver.solve()


def write_result(path: str, model: Optional[list[int]]) -> None:
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        if model is None:
            handle.write("UNSAT\n")
        else:
            handle.write("SAT\n")
            handle.write(format_model(model))
            handle.write("\n")


def main(argv: Optional[list[str]] = None) -> int:
    arguments = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    if len(arguments) != 2:
        print("Usage: python satsolver_blaze.py input.cnf output.txt", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    input_path, output_path = arguments
    try:
        num_vars, clauses = parse_dimacs_file(input_path)
        model = solve_cnf(num_vars, clauses)
        if model is not None and not model_satisfies(clauses, model):
            raise RuntimeError("Internal error: produced model does not satisfy the input CNF")
        write_result(output_path, model)
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - CLI safety path
        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
``````
